Well, they do but personally I would never buy a CVT myself.
Because being efficient doesn't also mean being reliable. They can go out at 50,000 miles and are expensive to repair.
Prontisimo!
Actually evidence suggests that MCNs are a complete joke and they provide nothing that you can't acquire on your own. Have fun giving away a portion of your revenue for nothing...

This response needs to be stickied somewhere because it can be used for like 90% of the threads I read on here. Your family and core audience thinks your videos are awesome. Great, and? Just because you worked hard on something and did all the right things doesn't mean someone isn't doing it better than you. Life isn't fair. Everyone should get used to it.
Not sure if serious...
The idea is to create content so good that *other* people share your content on reddit for you.
Would also like to know
Ships in three weeks...thanks anyway though.
It's all good. Amazon is almost out again now too.
Maybe people don't want to watch videos about your lifestyle and sports? 🤔

*sits down*

Hi I'm detective Stone with the Meadowbrook police department. What are you doing here??

I don't have a strong option on any of that but I sure as hell do that 10 minute bullshit. If I search for something I see a video thats between 10 and 11 minutes? Nope. I'm looking somewhere else. You won't get a click from me no matter how relevant it is.

It's lazy as hell. Give me 3 more minutes of solid content instead of doing the absolute bare minimum to stretch your 6 minute tutorial to 10:04. Go fuck yourself you greedy bastard.
Now
Where?!
No worries, thank you!
Well first off how many is "heaps"?
Why would you do that when you can focus on making good content and let YouTube promote it for free?

So, it seems exciting yes, and I would go nuts seeing that too BUT he even says in that post that they don't have to watch your content, just subscribe. So I would imagine a large percentage of them will do just that, nothing.

So what does that really get you in the end? A bunch of dead subs if you ask me.
Yes. It is. It's tag spamming.
Lol. Right...

Here's what's up. Making ten minute videos can absolutely be detrimental to the success of your video. Why? Because the algorithm follows people. Big YouTubers do it to increase revenue, so smaller channels just started copying them. 

If I see a video that's 10:04 I keep scrolling. It doesn't matter if its relevant to what I want to watch. It comes off as lazy and greedy, and like they did the absolute bare minimum to stretch that video out. 9 minutes? I'll watch. 12? Yup. But screw that lazy 10 minute  nonsense. 

Since the algorithm follows people, people like me who hate that will keep scrolling, telling the algorithm that people aren't into that video, lowering its likelyhood of being recommended more often.

No. No it isn't. Your video has nothing to do with that creator so using their name in your tags is in fact both spamming AND misleading. It doesn't matter if your video is related to theirs, is it ABOUT them? No? Then it's against the rules.

 False information like this is exactly the reason why you see someone complaining that their channel was "unfairly deleted" every single day on reddit.
Yeah don't do anything that makes it easy to steal your content. Which is that. Either be in the video or use your normal voice. Those are musts when starting in 2019.
I could make a video titled stylish dad is the coolest youtuber ever and rank number 1 for that tag. Problem is no one's searching for that.

Do you watch every single channel that gets deleted or something?

You should Google misleading tags. Have fun with your deleted channel.

Misleading Metadata or Thumbnails: Using the title, thumbnails, description, or *tags* to trick users into believing the content is something it is not.


Straight from Google genius. I'm pretty over arguing with you. Deuces!
Really. Rob from Vid IQ recommended putting Pewdiepie in your tags in order to grow more? Holy goodness you're delusional. Good day sir.

You're that "algorithm guru" who thought that because their video was being recommended for an hour that they had made it on YouTube...

My channel is monetized, has been for 2 years now, wasn't affected one bit by any of the adpocalypse issues, nor the new monetization requirements. 

And me seeing 10 minute videos as greedy means I don't understand how they work...how? Did you...did you even read my post? Your English reading comprehension must be as bad as your writing comprehension...
A good example is The Great War. It was an awesome ride for 4 years but then they got to the end of the war and ran out of content. Now what?

Oh boy impromptu channel reviews! Here's what's up. You've made almost 400 videos in order to gain 25k subscribers. And a reaction channel at that. More on that in a sec. 

My channel actually has almost 2 million views. Why the discrepancy? Because a lot of them are private now because they don't fit my niche. I started in the men's tailoring niche about 2 months ago and have had more growth in a month than I have in the last 2 years combined. Setting those to private was hard but worth it. I'm planning for the long haul, not jumping from trend to trend to sustain my channel. That's foolish.

But yes, Lets use *social blade* to determine the growth and health of someones channel, because that's accurate. My thumbnails are fine. Why do I know this? Because I have a healthy click through rate. Analytics you don't have access to. I don't need to use the "OMG I ALMOST DIED" face on my thumbnails to get clicks. 

A reaction channel, yes because that's sustainable long term. You're a full-time content creator, and you rely on *ads*. Anyone and their mother would tell you not to rely on ads as your primary source of income. I created and treat my channel like a business. I make more from brand deals than most people make on adsense in 2 months. Ads are nice, but have fun when something out of your control causes you to be demonetized. You don't have to worry about that with brand deals and affiliate marketing. Wanna know how much I make from selling *sewing machines?*

You however (from the looks of it) rely soley on adsense and whatever the latest trend is. My content is evergreen. I don't need to jump on the latest K-Pop controversy, my content will grow with me forever. Trends come and go. Remember fidget spinner channels? Literally anyone would tell you not to put all your eggs in one basket and to diversify your income. 

And look at the damn camera when you're talking to it.
I was thinking the exact same thing...

You're welcome. Will you get caught? Honestly, probably not. 1000's of people do it. But what matters is you. What happens is someone gets their channel deleted over it and they *always* use the argument that "well I see other people doing it all the time". 

YouTube can change your life. Why waste your one shot on trying to find shortcuts that don't even work anyway. 

Go look up Tim Schmoyer. He said it best, if it seems easy to game then it doesn't work. The algorithm isn't stupid. It doesn't go "jee this person put Pewdiepie in their tags 5 times, this video must be about him and I should recommend this video next to *all* of his content..."
A month and a half. Do something different from everyone else and you can grow fast.
The algorithm changed a bit at the beginning of the year to promote your older content now. That's why a video can do nothing for a month and then jump into browse features and blow up.
*drops the mic*
And a *whole* lot of them...
Yeah make good unique content and let YouTube promote it for you.

Yes they do. They promote it when it helps then achieve their goals. Keep people on YouTube and watching for long periods of time. 

My channel grew more when I just focused on my content and stopped trying to spam my content on every subreddit that I could. Let YouTube do the hard work for you.
Same...

But it is...

I TOTALLY get it man, I was that guy who thought that if I just get as many links to my videos out there as possible then I can bring eyes to my content and I will grow faster. There's a problem with that, bringing eyes to your content isn't enough. You want to KEEP eyes on your content and keep eyes on YouTube. You know what most people do when they watch a YouTube video that was linked on Reddit? They go back to Reddit (or wherever they came from). That's on top of them watching for 30 seconds then clicking back. 

The algorithm then determines that your content is bad and doesn't show it to anyone. I would get some massive views upfront and then my videos would plummet like a rock the very next day. Every time. It wasn't until I said screw it, focused on ONE NICHE, and created content around that one niche that I started to grow. No more throwing links here and there and everywhere. The algorithm needs time to crunch the data and determine who would most want to watch your content. People on Reddit? They aren't your audience, they are most likely one of two people, similar content creators, or people who just want to casually browse Reddit and have no interest in your content basically because they know you have a hidden agenda. 

Your audience is on YouTube man, I'm telling ya.
It was at this moment that I realized reading a wall of text in all italics is incredibly uncomfortable...

Well let's start at the very beginning before you start promoting. Honest advice and real life stuff on...what? Who exactly are you trying to reach? Unless you know exactly who your content is for and why they should care I think you're gonna be sorely disappointed with your results.

I would narrow it down even more than that and focus on ONE of those topics and dive deep. You have to remember it's 2019, we're late to the party. There's channels dedicated to, crushing, and focusing only on each of those topics in depth.  

Wanna make a video on over coming anxiety? There's channels with hundreds of videos on it. Confidence? Same thing. You scatter your audience when you touch on too many topics. I know because I did it. People would subscribe for one video and  not watch anything else because there was nothing else like it on my channel. 

The idea is to get them on one video, and make them realize that there's *a lot* more content on your channel that interests them. If you do make videos about anxiety don't make one make like 13 and put them in a playlist...

They're recommending it now, you're just not getting hundreds of thousands of views like you want. 

And it doesn't matter how many videos you upload. You need to do something different. It's why you see people with hundreds of videos and like 250 subscribers. Those hundreds of videos aren't any different from the other 506 million Fortnite videos that YouTube has indexed. 

You can upload *two* videos and get insane traction.

items.title: Your audience ISN'T on Reddit, they're on YOUTUBE! So Why "promote" here?

items.text:
Well think about it and put yourself in a viewer's shoes. I wouldn't watch any of your videos until the end. Ever. Why? Because all I'm doing is seeing if that particular track fits for what I want to use it for. And that takes 10-30 seconds to determine. It's gonna be a hard road for you because content like that doesn't really match with long viewing durations like YouTube wants.

I say all of that because before I used epidemic sounds that's exactly what I did. I wasn't looking to like or subscribe or turn on notifications. I wouldn't have cared when you posted. If I needed something I would search for it, not wait for you to release something.

I'll play devils advocate and say did Markiplier desperately share it himself or did *someone else* share it for him?

And copying what big YouTubers do is like the number one thing you shouldn't do. That's like me going out and buying a Red Dragon camera so I can be like Peter McKinnon. My content sucks compared to his just like most people's lets plays suck compared to markiplier's.
You're honestly spot on. BUT "tackling other social media platforms" usually means use it as a link dumping ground and getting mad when your IG followers don't leave IG to watch your videos....

Where did I say they don't use other platforms? 

And please, plenty of people know how the algorithm works. It isn't some all knowing mysterious AI...

Here's a video by Roberto Blake. https://youtu.be/P6g2QbXTpL4

You! I just made a post about you. You said my thumbnails sucked and at first I was mad but then I was like "wait...they do, I wouldn't click on this..."

I spent all weekend changing like 40 of them lol. Thought that was funny, thanks for bringing it to my attention. And sorry for being so argumentative and judgmental of your channel!
But see you're using it exactly as you should, as a separate platform. You use IG the way you should, by creating separate content for it and not using it as a link dumping ground.

I STRONGLY suggest you educate yourself before you come in here putting me or anyone on blast man, because you're making yourself look foolish. Like I already said, the algorithm(s) aren't some mysterious AI. The employees don't know how it works? Are you serious? Who do you think MADE the AI dude? God? 

The algorithm absolutely isn't for the viewers, why would they care? Tim Schmoyer doesn't know how the algorithm works, riiiiight.

Daryl Eves has created dozens of channels with a combined million subscribers and gives hour long talks at Vidsummit about exactly how the algorithm works and what it's looking for. But nope, he doesn't know either, it's mysterious. 

The only people who say that it's a mystery are the ones who use it as an excuse for their content being surfaced, when in reality it's because their content is no different from the 54 million other indexed videos about Fortnite. Get outta here with that nonsense man.

The algorithm will promote videos that keep people watching for long periods of time. That's it. It follows people, and there patterns. It promotes  videos that achieve this and demotes videos that take people off of YouTube.

It depends on how much data you have man. A 30% click through rate seems great until you realize it's on 100 impressions...

Plus your click through rate is ONE of about a million different data points that the algorithms use to determine whether or not to promote your content. Don't look at it as the end all be all. Create content for viewers, not robots.
Ok dude 👍

You can disagree if you want but it doesn't make it not true. That's super dope that you got traction on Reddit man it really is. But you're thinking about your experience, not the other hundreds if not thousands of creators who try the same thing and fail.
That's what sucks, putting SEO and best practices together. SO MANY PEOPLE spout of foolish information, or info that worked in 2011 and is horribly out dated now.

Thanks for the feedback man. My click through rate isn't TERRIBLE, but it can always be better right? It hovers around 5.5% with about a million impressions or so, which is probably like...an 1/8th of what you get haha.

The thing about thumbnails that I dropped the ball on is looking at them in the creator studio and judging them as a WHOLE. Together they worked fine, but no one views my channel like that but...me. None of my thumbnails held their own at all, they got washed out on the sidebar, hell I could barely notice them. That's something I didn't really think about, don't optimize your thumbnails for your channel page and for search, but also SUGGESTED too. How do your thumbnails look on the side bar? As a whole they worked, but individually on the side bar they were drown out for sure. 

And that kinda freaked me out at first too until I realized what was going on. You can have a high click through rate until YouTube starts suggesting your content to people who might not be interested. It's hard to not panic, but it isn't a bad thing, that means they're finding an audience for you. 

I didn't think about changing them after a week either...hmmm. That's a great idea because my dumbass is all like "well, it's 3% now but it will get better right?" Nope, it doesn't lol. That's a solid tip man, thanks!
Agreed. To everyone disagreeing with me and telling me that Reddit is the best way to give your content a "boost" just read this post.

Man those are some damn impressive numbers! Text is very hit or miss, and it completely depends on the niche. What's hard is even slight variations in a niche can change whether or not text is effective or not. I feel like for you guys it would be redundant. People are coming there for the singer and your reaction, so the only thing text could provide is maybe an emphasis on your thoughts. For example if there was a Kpop singer who came out of nowhere and had a solid debut (I know nothing about Kpop, forgive me lol) you could say something like "impressive..." or "surprisingly impressive". Just my thoughts. 

I am so torn over the shocked face and emotional face movement. In some ways it's SUPER effective, but again it depends on the niche. What I notice is that some people are super awkward about it. I don't know if you know who Brian G Johnson is (I'm sure you do) but he's a guy who's thumbnails scream "this totally isn't my personality but shocked face thumbnails are effective". They just look...awkward and uncomfortable if that makes sense? Look them up, it's kinda funny. 

You saw the EXACT same video from Vid IQ that I did lol, I saw Rob giving examples of his thumbnails and how they've changed, and the new ones are WAY better than his old ones. Even looking at mine, it makes me lead more towards the zoomed face because you're right, the text takes over. There are a few where it's OK but anything more than two or three words means it's hard to figure out where the eye should be drawn too, ya know? You've mentioned the Avenger thumb a few times now, so I took the hint and just spent an hour on it lol. Let me know what you think.
Focus on your content and let YouTube promote it for you.

Thanks man on the feedback for the thumbnail! And you're right about the blood association, I didn't think about that haha. 

I go back and forth SO MUCH over the zoomed in face thing but you're spot on, it takes 5 minutes to search successful channels to notice they all have one thing in common, zoomed in faces, so if it aint broke don't fix it. 

I wanna try AB testing as well, because sometimes I will change my title or thumbnail to something that I assume is better, but it always isn't ya know? I heard YouTube is rolling one out but we will see...

I use Photoshop. I HATED it at first, I will never forget when I first attempted it because I couldn't figure out jack shit. I have the creative cloud, and while it sucks having to pay $50 a month it's finally worth it now as I use everything that comes with it. There are a ton of free ones out there but I don't like them as much. GIMP I heard is good but it's even more difficult than Photoshop to me...

I hear ya on not wanting to drop cash on something like that though, I struggle with what and how much to pour into my channel all the time. Plus it depends on whether or not I get a sponsor that month or not too, I could load one into every damn video but then people wouldn't watch anymore, so it's a delicate balance...

I like the second one A LOT more, but if you could combine them it would be PERFECT! Your faces show so much more emotion in the second ones! I noticed something that a lot of people kinda drop the ball on too, your lighting. You're using Rembrant lighting where the lights are more on the side of you, I would say have them front and center so that your faces are evenly light, and if you have access to an editing software I would change the colors a bit as well to make them pop even more. If you don't send me that raw image and I can edit it for you in a few minutes if you want too. I'm not a master, but Photoshop and Lightroom make it pretty easy!  Just let me know! Funny how we came full circle, we hated each other a week ago lol.
Water resistance =\= water PROOF.
Apparently not since people keep using proof in place of resistance...
Seriously?? She looks 21...

Totally see what you mean, looking at the thumbnails as a whole with context, I don't notice the lighting issues at all. You gotta work with what you got, I totally get that man. My favorite is the Gong Linna thumbnail, your face has some sharpness to it where your wrinkles are, and the facial expression makes it just different enough that it doesn't look like you're re-using the same face every time. That isn't a bad thing, and a TON of people do that, but I'm personally not a fan. It looks too mass produced then. 

You guys do a good job with color too, I see what you mean about text, it would look too crowded with text. With your channel I think what probably works best is who you're reacting to and how you feel about it with your facial expressions. 

I'm even struggling now with making my face just different enough so that it doesn't look the same every time haha. Thumbnails are an art though, and I was browsing last night specifically looking at thumbnails and noticed that everyone really does have a face on there. The ones that didn't looked kinda weird to me...
Also wait longer than 7 hours to determine whether or not a video is successful...
Was thinking the same thing...

I could see that but I wouldn't think anime character personally, I just think strong emotion. There's one guy who uses his face in his thumbnails and it's him making a generic slight smile, in every single one, literally all of them are the same photo. And yet he has 200k subscribers, blows my mind. 

I should start doing more tests like that. I and a lot of other people need to look at what's working more than look for the next best thing to make. What works are actual hands on tutorials where you don't see me but hear me behind the camera doing something. I get it and it makes sense but I don't like tutorials like that I feel like they're too impersonal, I wanna see the person AND what it is that they're doing. 

But back to thumbnails, the struggle is real I know lol. I still can't believe that a week ago at this time I had thumbnails on my channel that I thought were great, when in reality they couldn't have been worse. I don't know if you use dark mode on YouTube but make your thumbnails around that too. I use it and think its amazing so I made my thumbs with a lot of whites thinking that they stood out more. Well not many people use dark mode so when I would look in incognito mode they looked really boring and didn't stand out at all.

You are totally overthinking it and no one will notice.

That being said dropping the the gives it a much better sound, I like it a lot!

Oh I bet that is hard as hell. I'm glad that my content doesn't revolve around other peoples content, because every single day I see posts on Reddit from people claiming fair use when they don't actually understand how it works...

BUT that being said, a TON of huge channels use it successfully that's for sure.

Dark mode turns all of the white elements black, and the text white. It's AMAZING!!

And Butthead rocks man lol

Completely agree with you. Let's be honest, most people think their friends and family care a lot more than they actually do. 

They don't care any more than you care when your friends get a new job or start a new business venture. You just see it as spam on your news feed.
Truth. Sorry for your loss :(
Thank you so much!!!
No way?!?

Yes, you're missing the millions of other metrics the algorithms use to determine whether or not to surface and promote a video. It's very good at showing the right content to the right person at the right time. Focusing on click through rate and audience retention are only two metrics, and they are super deceiving. I've had videos with "bad" metrics do great, and videos with awesome metrics (audience retention and a high click through rate) sit there doing nothing for months. 

It all comes down to your content and how people react to it.

Don't assume you're fine with fair use. It's not about the length of the clip you use its about what you do with it. Did you transform it and make it your own by adding commentary or changing the clip at all?
Clickbait isn't the same as misleading clickbait. Newspapers have used clickbait for over 100 years.
I'm almost positive selling your account is against the ToS.
